tabela: Situation
Observation feedback to a teacher who works in English only, and who is free to disagree.
Opening with what you saw
What I noticed was… · From where I was sitting…
Recommending so he can refuse
One thing you might try is… · It might be worth… · Have you thought about…?
Holding it under disagreement
That is fair — and the part I would still look at is… · I might be wrong about the reason. What I saw was…
Asking, and meaning it
What were you trying to do at that point? · How did that feel from where you were?
Key vocabulary
to push back · that is fair · to have a point · to act on something

callout.texto:
Could he say no, because… and still be talking about the same thing?
If yes, you left him room. If the only answers are yes or a fight, you gave an instruction — however politely it was worded.

abertura: Record a short voice message, if you would like to.

callout.texto:
Think of feedback you have to give in the next few weeks — to a teacher, or to anyone whose work you have watched.

What you are trying to do: say it in a way the person could answer. Start with what you saw, and finish with something they choose.

fourmovesina.titulo: Four moves in a feedback conversation
abertura: Use this whenever you want to review what you did in class.

tabela: Opening on the observation
What I noticed was…
Starting on the verdict means he defends before he listens.
Asking first
What were you trying to do at that point?
Your recommendation answers a question he never had.
Recommending refusably
One thing you might try…
He agrees in the room and changes nothing after it.
Holding under disagreement
That is fair — and the part I would still look at is…
Either the point disappears, or the conversation becomes about who is right.
